equation_request.abstract: Bernstein-Vazirani algorithm (the one-query algorithm) can identify a completely specified linear Boolean function using a single query to the oracle with certainty. The first aim of the paper is to show that if the provided Boolean function is affine, then one more query to the oracle (the two-query algorithm) is required to identify the affinity of the function with certainty. The second aim of the paper is to show that if the provided Boolean function is incompletely defined, then the one-query and the two-query algorithms can be used as bounded-error quantum polynomial algorithms to identify certain classes of incompletely defined linear and affine Boolean functions respectively with probability of success at least $2/3$.

specification.problem: Given a standard XOR oracle U_f|x>|y>=|x>|y xor f(x)> for f(x)=a.x xor b on n bits, recover a with one BV query and decide linear (b=0) versus affine non-linear (b=1) with a second query. Incompletely defined variant: f is known only on a subset D of {0,1}^n, and the BV output distribution is used as a bounded-error test.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest construction: n=2 (3 qubits for query 1; the second-query circuit uses n+1 qubits or fewer), fully defined affine f, two queries, deterministic. The incompletely-defined-domain case is given only as the output-distribution formula under an assumed promise class. The precise classes of incompletely defined functions in the paper, and the proof of the 2/3 bound, are outside scope.

symbols.meaning: defined subset of inputs for an incompletely defined f
measured n-bit string from the BV query
known defined input used in the second query (0^n if defined)

equations.label: XOR oracle
equations.description: Standard oracle acting on n input qubits and one target qubit.
equations.justification: Standard oracle model; the sketch assumes it, and the abstract only mentions queries to the oracle.
assumptions: Standard XOR oracle with an ancilla target

equations.label: BV output state, fully defined affine f
equations.description: With the target in |->, the oracle gives phase (-1)^{f(x)}. After the final H^n the input register is |a> up to a global phase (-1)^b, so s=a with certainty and b is unobservable from query 1.
equations.justification: Standard BV analysis extended to the affine case. The abstract implies one query is not enough to identify affinity, consistent with b being a global phase.

equations.label: Second query reads offset
equations.description: Measuring the target gives b=f(0). The function is linear iff b=0 and affine non-linear iff b=1.
equations.justification: The abstract says one more query is needed. Evaluating f(0) is one proposed way to use it, and the paper's actual second query may differ.
assumptions: Computational-basis evaluation counts as a query

equations.label: Offset from any defined point
equations.description: If 0^n is undefined, use the measured s=a and a defined point x_0 to compute b classically.
equations.justification: Follows from f(x)=a.x xor b once a is known. Requires f(x_0) from a query.

equations.label: BV output distribution on partial domain
equations.description: Undefined inputs contribute zero amplitude. The method succeeds if P(a) is at least 2/3 and a is the most probable string.
equations.abstract_quote: with probability of success at least $2/3$
equations.justification: The abstract claims bounded-error success on certain classes of incompletely defined functions. The formula is the natural BV distribution with undefined terms dropped, and the sketch states it.

registers.name: x
registers.role: input register, measured to give s; Qiskit classical bit i holds s_i, so read counts keys reversed

registers.name: t
registers.role: oracle target; |-> in query 1, |0> in query 2 where f(0) is read directly

specification.initial_state: Query 1: |0^n>|1> with H on all qubits, giving |+^n>|->. Query 2: |0^n>|0>.

steps.description: Query 1: prepare target in |->, apply H^n to the input register, apply the oracle once, apply H^n, measure the input register to get s=a. Reverse the counts key to index bits.
Query 2: on |0^n>|0> apply the oracle once and measure the target to get b=f(0). Decide linear if b=0, affine non-linear if b=1.
If 0^n is undefined, query a defined x_0 and compute b classically from s.
Partial-domain case: run the same BV circuit and take the most frequent s from the histogram.

specification.measurement: Query 1: measure the n input qubits in the computational basis. Query 2: measure the target qubit. Use little-endian reversal when reading s.
specification.classical_postprocessing: a=s (most frequent string for partial domains). b=f(0), or f(x_0) xor s.x_0. Output linear if b=0, otherwise affine non-linear.
assumptions: Second query is a computational-basis evaluation at a known defined point
Promise class for partial domains is not specified, only assumed to give P(a)>=2/3
missing_information: Exact classes of incompletely defined linear and affine functions
The paper's actual second-query circuit, which may differ from evaluating f(0)
Proof or threshold for the 2/3 bound
How undefined inputs are implemented in the oracle
